constraints: Pure refactor; the Editor class keeps every public member with the same signature, and Object.keys(new Editor()) keeps the same names and order.

New modules have no module-level side effects other than constants; no regex splitting of long strings, deep recursion, per-operation closures or handler tables (the native CLI runs the code in Boa).
Moved and new packages/core code type-checks with noUncheckedIndexedAccess (design command 8).

Load-tolerant gates (design D11): mise run verify and mise run test-cli run only inside the design's three-attempt sh -c loops; command 10 runs directly after the test-cli loop. If all three attempts fail, the gate fails; it is never waived as load.
Every verification command exits 0 once its plan's changes are in; native parity is verified only through mise run test-cli (design D9); there is no standalone parity run.
Every plan declares artifactRoots ["target"]; every file a plan edits is in its writePaths (docs/development.md for sms-01 and sms-02, apps/cli/native/README.md for sms-03).
Strictly typed code in the surrounding style; no emojis; cargo with CARGO_TERM_QUIET=true; no tool attribution in commits.
designDecisionsAndRationale: D1-D6 reused unchanged (class chain, component members in Editor, lowest-chain-class planner types, Batch class with module-level handlers and the switch in Batch.apply, parity topic files with a non-test harness, focused tests only for newly extracted helpers).

D11: verify and test-cli each get up to three attempts and pass on the first fully green attempt, whose log is copied to verify.log or test-cli.log; a CPU-time check with a 15% limit against 0.8.5 guards against real slowdowns; deadlines and timeouts are unchanged.

intentionalTradeoffs: Single-inheritance class chain (at most six levels) instead of delegation stubs (D1, Risks).
Component and responsive-variant members stay in Editor, the last chain class (D2).
Batch members used by handlers (record, resolveReferences, boundsOf, targets, shape, moveBoxTo, lastPlaced) lose private; Batch and handlers stay unexported from edit-command.ts (design 2.2).
add-page keeps its own unchecked refs.set instead of batch.record, so no new error case is introduced (design 2.3).
Only newly extracted helpers get focused tests (D6).

Gates retry up to three times under load instead of loosening deadlines; the CPU-time check (also up to three attempts, reference measured right before the new binary) catches real slowdowns that a lucky green attempt could hide (D11).
If the 0.8.5 reference binary is missing, workers stop with a blocker and the orchestrator builds the b52e4db reference; workers never create git worktrees.
